items.title: Leslie Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: Kid Thomas I believe, he had a band that he called the Dixieland band, the Kid Thomas Dixieland Band.

ctx.x: Now do you think that picture in your mind makes it harder to promote this music?

Yeah. The tricky part of this is Dixieland was actually a fine term way back when both black and white bands used that term. It wasn’t just a white band that used the term Dixieland, a lot of the black bands did use it. Kid Thomas I believe, he had a band that he called the Dixieland band, the Kid Thomas Dixieland Band. That was not a bad word. What happened was it became more of associated with the novelty music or ice cream © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

social type music rather than serious improvisational jazz. It became a music where the solo was passed around rather than ensembling. And that, you just change the whole meaning of that word. And what you have, quite frankly, were people that formed a Dixieland band who could only play a little, not a lot. And so it took on a bad connotation where there were some musicians who didn’t want to be associated with that word at all, you’d never use that word around Wild Bill Davison for instance.
